card.title: The Object Changes Meaning
card.instruction: Choose one ordinary detail and reinterpret it as gift, threat, evidence, or symbol as the scene evolves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I gave you that key because you were welcome here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then why are you holding it like evidence?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because the cupboard was locked before the cake disappeared.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I brought you a replacement cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then perhaps the key is a subscription. We'll discuss the terms over tea.

mechanism: A changes a key from welcome to evidence of theft and then a proposed ongoing cake arrangement.
confusable: Unlike replacing one prop with another, the same detail must carry distinct meanings as B adds facts.
comparison: S239-a reinterprets access as a subscription; S239-b reinterprets travel tickets as a future invitation.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
